title: Bhikkhus, regarding the precepts that are unbroken, unblemished, unspotted, untarnished, leading to liberation, praised by the wise, not clung to, conducive to concentration — a…
content: Bhikkhus, regarding the precepts that are unbroken, unblemished, unspotted, untarnished, leading to liberation, praised by the wise, not clung to, conducive to concentration — a bhikkhu lives possessing such precepts in common with his fellow celibates, both in private and in public. This principle of cordiality creates affection, creates respect, leading to cohesion, to non-dispute, to harmony, to unity.

title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, good associates. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, good associates. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is easy to speak to, possessing qualities that make him easy to admonish, patient, and well-receptive to instruction. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, for whatever duties his fellow celibates have to do, whether great or small, he is skillful and diligent, possessing the right consideration of means, able to do and to organize. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu loves the Dhamma, speaks pleasantly, rejoices greatly in the supreme Dhamma and supreme Discipline. This, bhikkhus, is a quality that constitutes a guardian.

title: Elder Lomasakaṅgiya: With my chest, I will push back the grass — dabba, kusa, munja, pabbaja. From my chest, I will push them away, I…
content:
Elder Lomasakaṅgiya:

With my chest, I will push back the grass — dabba, kusa, munja, pabbaja.
From my chest, I will push them away, I will develop the practice of solitary seclusion.

title: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who lives in too much association with families. What five? He constantly sees women; through seeing,…
content: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who lives in too much association with families. What five? He constantly sees women; through seeing, there is association; through association, there is intimacy; through intimacy, there is opportunity (for sexual intercourse); when the mind has been corrupted, it is to be expected that he will not delight in living the holy life, or he will fall into a corrupt offense, or he will give up the training and return to the lay life. Bhikkhus, these are the five dangers for a bhikkhu who lives in too much association with families.

title: Possessing five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who approaches families is loved, liked, respected, and an example for those families. What five? He does not become…
content: Possessing five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who approaches families is loved, liked, respected, and an example for those families. What five? He does not become intimate with those who are not confident, does not interfere where he has no authority, does not associate with opposing factions, does not whisper in private, and does not ask for too much. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who approaches families is loved, liked, respected, and an example for those families.

title: And, bhikkhus, what are formations? There are these three formations, bhikkhus: bodily formation, verbal formation, mental formation. These three, bhikkhus, are called formations.
content: And, bhikkhus, what are formations? There are these three formations, bhikkhus: bodily formation, verbal formation, mental formation. These three, bhikkhus, are called formations.

title: Not associating with fools, associating with the wise, Honoring those worthy of honor — this is the supreme blessing. Dwelling in a suitable place, having…
content:
Not associating with fools, associating with the wise,
Honoring those worthy of honor — this is the supreme blessing.

Dwelling in a suitable place, having made merit in the past,
Directing oneself rightly — this is the supreme blessing.

Having much learning, skilled in craft, well-trained in discipline,
Speaking well-spoken words — this is the supreme blessing.

Supporting one's mother and father, cherishing one's wife and children,
Having an unconfused livelihood — this is the supreme blessing.

title: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and sorrow, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna,…
content: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and sorrow, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which has neither pain nor pleasure, and is purified by equanimity and mindfulness. He sits suffusing his body with a pure, bright mind, so that no part of his entire body is not suffused with that pure, bright mind.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, a spear with a sharp blade. Then a person comes and says: 'With my hand or fist, I will bend this sharp…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, a spear with a sharp blade. Then a person comes and says: 'With my hand or fist, I will bend this sharp spear blade double, I will fold it back, I will twist it.' What do you think, bhikkhus, could that person, with his hand or fist, bend that sharp spear blade double, fold it back, twist it?" - "No, Venerable Sir." - "Why is that?" - "Venerable Sir, it is not easy to bend that sharp spear blade double, fold it back, twist it, without causing himself fatigue and affliction." - "So too, bhikkhus, for one who develops and cultivates the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, makes it his vehicle, makes it his base, establishes it, accumulates it, and properly undertakes it — any non-human who might think he could overthrow such a mind would only get tired and afflicted. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train thus: 'We will develop the liberation of mind by loving-kindness, cultivate it, make it our vehicle, make it our base, establish it, accumulate it, and properly undertake it.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train.

title: From a basis, suffering arises. All the various sufferings in the world arise from a basis. The fool, because of ignorance, creates the basis, Thus…
content:
From a basis, suffering arises.
All the various sufferings in the world arise from a basis.
The fool, because of ignorance, creates the basis,
Thus repeatedly encountering suffering.
Therefore, a wise person should not create a basis,
Contemplating the existence of birth and suffering.

Those who fall into the round of birth and death,
Going from this existence to that existence,
Their destination is due to ignorance.

This great ignorance leads to long wandering.
Beings who have attained true knowledge go no further.
